text:
vivian: following up on control-plane separation discussion — one sharp tradeoff: direct-to-anchor (clients talk IP:port/quic to regional anchor) vs a lightweight proxy layer in-customer-vpc. thoughts?
omar: direct is simpler and lower latency but harder for IP-whitelist customers. proxy lets us present stable egress IPs and do transparent TLS termination.
lee: proxy adds cost and NAT state. for high-throughput inference, proxy can become a hotspot. Could we make proxy optional per-customer profile?
sara: agree optional. also: QUIC vs TCP+TLS for anchor comms. QUIC gives better connection resumption across migrations and avoids TCP handoff pain during failover. downside: more complex infra and middlebox compatibility.
omar: QUIC would help stream resumption for KV windows. We can expose a ticket-based resumption token so clients can reconnect to a new anchor and pick up where they left off.
vivian: security note: resumption tokens must be bound to anchor_id + expiry + nonce. revoke should be immediate on handoff. how do we broadcast revocations to private installs?
sara: for Private, include a short-lived CRL that ops can push via controlplane sync; clients should check revocation on resume if they can reach controlplane, otherwise fail-safe to full bootstrap.
lee: discovery nuance: if using proxy mode, DNS can point to stable VIP; for direct mode we need SRV or SNI-based controlplane routing to pick region. SNI routing is neat — one TLS name with anchor as SNI. That avoids DNS TTL issues.
omar: SNI helps but not available for Private air-gapped customers without shared TLS infra. For those, local registry file or Env override still needed.
vivian: ops implications: proxies require LB automation and draining semantics. propose drain window: proxies accept existing streams and return 200 for health until connections < threshold then 503. mirror writes for handoff period when moving state between anchors.
sara: on mirroring: prefer idempotent write model where possible. If not, support compare-and-swap semantics at prefix level for critical updates, and allow a write mirror fallback for less-critical paths.
lee: metric requests: proxy_bytes_in/out, quic_resume_success, anchor_handoff_latency, proxy_cpu_percent. add anchor_id tag and peer_mode (direct/proxy).
vivian: opt-in config for customers: {"connect_mode":"auto|direct|proxy", "enable_quic":true, "resumption_ttl_s":300}. SDKs default to auto-> prefer direct unless customer whitelists IPs.
omar: ops-bot: perf spike scheduled: direct-quic vs proxy-tcp next Thu 04:00 UTC
sara: next steps: 1) vivian + lee write short spec for proxy vs direct with cost model, 2) omar prototype ticket-based resumption and QUIC perf numbers, 3) ops run perf spike and collect metrics.
vivian: will compile and attach to RFC follow-up. leaving thread open for comments.
